correctness.rationale: PASS: For a generic exposing functional on a tree-edge diamond sum, each summand chooses the endpoint with larger coordinate absolute value and its sign, inducing an acyclic orientation. Conversely any tree orientation is realizable by increasing positive weights along its directed edges, and its signed positive-indegree vector is uniquely exposed. Leaf peeling recovers the orientation from its unsigned indegrees, so the enumeration is bijective, without overcounting. Splitting by the bridge direction and t,s incoming leaf edges gives squared norm p+q−t−s+(t+epsilon)^2+(s+1−epsilon)^2, sign multiplicity 2^(p+q−t−s+1_{t+epsilon>0}+1_{s+1−epsilon>0}), producing F=A_p,1 A_q,0+A_p,0 A_q,1. At z=1 counts yield 8·3^(p+q)−2^(q+1)3^p−2^(p+1)3^q. Strict convexity of m−t+(t+delta)^2 locates outer endpoints; the ties at m=1 and p=q give contact counts 16,8,4 in their stated cases and R²=p²+q²+2max(p,q)+1. Central symmetry guarantees unique origin minimum ball and opposite-contact diameters. Independent finite direct orientation/endpoint sums for (1,1),(2,2),(2,3) reproduce 48/504/1584 vertices, R²=5/13/20 and contacts16/8/4.
